To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) monolingual and parallel corpora can be used to estimate translation probabilities, 2) comparable corpora can be leveraged to extract translation rules, and 3) the combination of monolingual, parallel, and comparable data improves the performance of SMT in low resource settings.
we have shown that it is possible to improve the performance in low resource conditions using monolingual and/or comparable corpora.

the following question: How can SMT be improved in the low resource setting, where only small amounts of high-quality parallel data are available?
the development of techniques for exploiting non-parallel data for statistical machine translation.
developing new methods for SMT that are more robust in low resource conditions, and which are applicable to more language pairs.
